Let me tell you why I think life is worth living.

I think life is worth living precisely because it allows you to see it for what it is: an endless struggle. You see it everyday in the tragedies of this world. Sickness, unbearable pain, degeneracy, straight up insanity; you name it. Because if I wasn't here to experience it, how else was I supposed to know?

I've come to realize that no matter what I do to make things better, it just makes things worse. Every need I fulfill leaves a void for another one to take its place.

Eventually, in the context of a pure thought experiment, I asked myself the following question: "If I could choose to exist, would I?"

The answer, as dark as it may seem, is a NEGATION.

I have now started to harvest my pain for my journey in the unknown. I plan on escaping this miserable world, and I won't be looking back.

Now, as I'm waiting for my death to come, I will be asking myself one question: "Just how bad can things get?"

I can only know the final answer on the instant of my death. My only hope is that this answer is strong enough to definitely disgust me for an eternity.

NIRVANA -which means "extinct" as an adjective- is where I'm heading. And I won't let this world hold me back.
